claims.text: Nano-scale oxide dispersoids delay dynamic recrystallization in tungsten-based plasma-facing alloys at high temperatures.
Nano-scale oxide dispersoids pin dislocations in tungsten alloys.
Nano-scale oxide dispersoids stabilize or pin grain boundaries in tungsten alloys.
Delaying dynamic recrystallization through dispersoid pinning enhances high-temperature plastic strain capacity.
Delaying dynamic recrystallization through dispersoid pinning enhances high-temperature toughness.
Introducing controlled amounts of nano-scale oxide dispersoids such as yttria can form a uniform dispersoid network when other processing parameters are held constant.
The relevant dispersoids are located both at grain boundaries and within the tungsten-alloy matrix.
Dispersoid-induced grain-boundary pinning retards grain growth during high-temperature deformation.
Inhibited dislocation mobility allows the material to sustain higher plastic strains without significant toughness loss.
Dispersoid-added samples will have a later onset of dynamic recrystallization than an otherwise identical dispersoid-free baseline.
Dispersoid-added samples will retain finer grains during high-temperature deformation than the baseline.
Dispersoid-added samples will exhibit greater high-temperature plastic strain capacity than the baseline.
Dispersoid-added samples will exhibit greater high-temperature fracture toughness than the baseline.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate above approximately 1200 °C under deformation conditions relevant to fusion plasma-facing applications.
The proposed mechanism may also apply to refractory-alloy systems similar to tungsten alloys.
Severe radiation damage may dominate microstructural evolution and limit the applicability of the proposed dispersoid mechanism.
The magnitude of changes in plastic strain and toughness may depend on dispersoid concentration and distribution.
The magnitude of changes in plastic strain and toughness may depend on prolonged operational exposure.
